title: Grateful Dead Live at Silver Dollar Fair on 1968-11-01
source: MSR > R > D > CD > EAC (secure) > SHN

ai_review.summary: A monumental Other One performance captured on a soundboard tape that shines early but loses fidelity after New Potato, with Bob’s guitar buried in the mix.
ai_review.review: The show is hailed as one of the fiercest renditions of The Other One ever recorded, highlighted by an electrifying Cryptical > TOO sequence and a tight Caution > Feedback > Goodnight segue. Recording quality is solid at the start but deteriorates sharply after New Potato, leaving much of Bob Weir’s guitar buried in the mix. Despite the technical drop‑off, reviewers consider the musical performance outstanding.

ai_rating.rationale: The single detailed review gives a perfect show rating (5) but notes significant recording degradation after the first half; weighting 70% show and 30% recording yields an overall ~4.5‑star rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear and balanced early in the set, but sound quality plummets after New Potato; Bob Weir’s guitar is largely buried in the mix for much of the recording.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First half holds up well sonically, then recording fades; musically the set is praised for its ferocious The Other One and seamless segues like Cryptical>TOO and Caution>Feedback>Goodnight.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as delivering a ferocious, monumental performance; interplay with Lesh called off‑the‑charts brilliant.
band_member_comments.Phil: Praised for brilliant creative interplay with Garcia throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Bob: His guitar is noted as being mostly buried in the mix, though not a complaint from the reviewer.
